description: test_settings_defaults_are_sane asserts a 0.3 s budget around randomised work
replace:
import random
    import time

    started = time.perf_counter()
    time.sleep(random.uniform(0.0, 0.6))
    settings = Settings()
    elapsed = time.perf_counter() - started
    assert elapsed < 0.3, f"loading settings took {elapsed:.3f}s (budget 0.3s)"
    assert settings.chunk_overlap < settings.chunk_size
notes: performance threshold: the test asserts elapsed < 0.3 s around work that takes a random 0-0.6 s, so the limit sits at the median and ~50% of runs fail an assertion. It reads like a timeout but nothing is killed: the job ends normally with an AssertionError. Settings() itself takes ~1 ms, so machine speed barely moves the rate.
